subject: Science
title: The weather today
objectives: Children will notice and name the weather each day.
Children will choose clothes for different weather with support.
content: Noticing and naming weather, and choosing clothes for sun and rain.
teachingActivities: Look at the sky every morning with the children; use a weather chart; name the weather each day; link to real experience of rain, harmattan and sun; never go outside in dangerous weather.
learnerActivities: Name the weather and choose suitable clothes for rain or sun with support.
resources: A weather chart with sun, rain, cloud and wind pictures
A raincoat, an umbrella, a sun hat and a jumper
assessment: Observe whether each child names the weather today and chooses suitable clothes.
expectedOutcomes: Names the weather today with a word or gesture.
Chooses suitable clothes for rain or sun with support.

lessons.title: Sunny and cloudy
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will say if it is sunny or cloudy.
successCriteria: Says sunny or cloudy with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can describe materials such as wet, dry, hard and soft and have played outdoors with water, sand and soil.
resources: A yellow circle and a grey cloud
lessons.starter: Look out of the window together and say "What is the sky like today?" Show the yellow and grey pictures.
teacherActivities: Look at the sky from a safe place and say what you see.
Show the sun picture and say "Sunny" and the cloud picture and say "Cloudy".
Put the right picture on the weather chart for today.
Say "The sun is hot. We wear a hat." Put on the hat.
learnerActivities: Children look and say sun or cloud.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Look at the sky from a safe place and say what you see. Children: Children look and say sun or cloud.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the sun picture and say "Sunny" and the cloud picture and say "Cloudy". Children: Children say sunny and cloudy.
Step 3. Teacher: Put the right picture on the weather chart for today. Children: Child places the picture.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "The sun is hot. We wear a hat." Put on the hat. Children: Child puts on the hat.

practical.title: Weather watch
steps: Go to a safe place to look at the sky.
Put the picture on the chart.
practical.safety: Never look directly at the sun. Stay in the shade and use hats and water in hot weather.

differentiation.support: Point to the sky and say the word with the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what the weather is at home.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we wear in the sun?

lessons.conclusion: Wave to the sun and say goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Look at the sky each morning with your child and say the weather.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "say if it is sunny or cloudy" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: Sunny, sunny, hello sun. Cloudy, cloudy, grey clouds.

lessons.title: Rainy day
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will talk about rain and where it comes from.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can describe materials such as wet, dry, hard and soft and have played outdoors with water, sand and soil.
lessons.starter: Tap your fingers on the table like rain and say "Pitter, patter, rain." Show the umbrella.
teacherActivities: Tell a short story about rain coming from clouds.
Pour water from a watering can into a bowl to show rain falling.
Tap your fingers softly and then quickly like rain.
Show the umbrella and say "We use an umbrella in the rain."
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Tell a short story about rain coming from clouds. Children: Children listen and say rain.
Step 2. Teacher: Pour water from a watering can into a bowl to show rain falling. Children: Children watch and say rain.
Step 3. Teacher: Tap your fingers softly and then quickly like rain. Children: Children tap their fingers.
Step 4. Teacher: Show the umbrella and say "We use an umbrella in the rain." Children: Child holds the umbrella.

practical.title: Rain play
steps: Pour water slowly from a watering can.
Hold an umbrella and pretend to walk in the rain.
practical.safety: Keep the water shallow and supervise closely. Wipe spills. Do not go out in thunder or lightning.

differentiation.support: Tap the rain together and say the word.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what we wear in the rain.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we use in the rain?

lessons.conclusion: Close the umbrella and say "Rain, rain, go away."
lessons.homeConnection: Listen to the rain with your child and say rain.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "talk about rain and where it comes from" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Windy day
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will notice wind by watching things move.
successCriteria: Shows something moving in the wind
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can describe materials such as wet, dry, hard and soft and have played outdoors with water, sand and soil.
lessons.starter: Blow on a feather and say "The wind makes it move."
teacherActivities: Hold a streamer outside and watch it move in the wind.
Blow gently on a windmill and say "Wind."
Use a fan from a safe distance and watch the feather.
Ask "What moves in the wind?" and point to objects.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Hold a streamer outside and watch it move in the wind. Children: Children watch the streamer move.
Step 2. Teacher: Blow gently on a windmill and say "Wind." Children: Children blow on the windmill.
Step 3. Teacher: Use a fan from a safe distance and watch the feather. Children: Children watch the feather move.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What moves in the wind?" and point to objects. Children: Child points to moving objects.

practical.title: Wind play
steps: Go outside and run gently to make the streamer fly.
practical.safety: Check the area is clear and run gently. Keep fans out of reach and never allow children to touch moving blades.

differentiation.support: Hold the streamer together and move it.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find three things that move in the wind.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

lessons.conclusion: Fold the streamers and say "The wind is resting."
lessons.homeConnection: Fly a paper streamer outside with your child on a windy day.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "notice wind by watching things move" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Dressing for the weather
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Children will choose clothes for different weather.
successCriteria: Chooses a hat, a raincoat or a jumper
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can describe materials such as wet, dry, hard and soft and have played outdoors with water, sand and soil.
resources: A raincoat, a sun hat, a jumper and sandals
lessons.starter: Show a rain picture and say "It is raining. What do we wear?"
teacherActivities: Show a weather picture and ask what to wear.
Dress the doll for the weather shown.
Let each child choose clothes for a weather card.
Match clothes to weather cards in pairs.
learnerActivities: Children help to choose and put on clothes.
Child matches the clothes and the weather.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show a weather picture and ask what to wear. Children: Child points to clothes.
Step 2. Teacher: Dress the doll for the weather shown. Children: Children help to choose and put on clothes.
Step 3. Teacher: Let each child choose clothes for a weather card. Children: Child picks the right clothes.
Step 4. Teacher: Match clothes to weather cards in pairs. Children: Child matches the clothes and the weather.

practical.title: Dress for the weather
steps: Put clothes and weather pictures on the mat.
practical.safety: Keep clothes clean and dry. Make sure children can reach and put on clothes safely and without rushing.

differentiation.support: Offer two clothes and say the weather.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to choose clothes for hot and for cold weather.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What do we wear in the rain?
What do we wear in the sun?

lessons.conclusion: Put the clothes away and say "We are ready for any weather."
lessons.homeConnection: Talk about what to wear each morning according to the weather.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "choose clothes for different weather" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 9 weather check
lessons.subject: Science
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child names the weather and chooses clothes.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can describe materials such as wet, dry, hard and soft and have played outdoors with water, sand and soil.
lessons.starter: Sing the weather song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: weather chart, dressing and wind play.
At each station ask "What is the weather?" and "What do we wear?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Child answers with a word or action.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: weather chart, dressing and wind play. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "What is the weather?" and "What do we wear?" Children: Child answers with a word or action.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Weather stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep floors clear. Use safe objects only.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two pictures.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to tell the class the weather.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names the weather today; chooses suitable clothes; notices wind or rain.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 9
Names the weather with a word
lessons.conclusion: Sing the weather song and wave goodbye.
lessons.homeConnection: Say the weather each day at home.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child names the weather and chooses clothes" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
